cards.text: Genesis 5 is a family album from Adam, the first man, down to Noah, and man after man lives hundreds of years and then he died, except Enoch. "Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away." Methuselah tops the list at 969 years, which is a LOT of birthday candles, and the line comes down to Noah, father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
Turn the page, friend: men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them. That family album is gonna need a SECOND album.

cards.question: The sons of God see that the daughters of men are beautiful. What do the sons of God do?

answers.text: Take as wives whomever they choose
Wait for the LORD to choose for them
Ask the fathers for their permission

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks, and friend, this is NOT a "hey, how was your week" kind of talk. He says His Spirit will not contend with man forever.

cards.question: The LORD says His Spirit will not contend with man forever. What reason does He give?
Then the LORD says that man's days shall be ___ years.

cards.text: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and afterward as well. The sons of God and the daughters of men have children together, and friend, this photo album just got a WHOLE lot more interesting.

cards.question: The sons of God and the daughters of men have children. Who do those children become?

cards.text: And here, friend, the story turns. The LORD looks at man on the earth, and I'm holding my breath like the junk drawer just slid open.

cards.question: What does the LORD see in man that is great upon the earth?
The LORD sees that every inclination of the thoughts of man's heart is altogether ___ all the time.
The LORD sees great wickedness in man. How does the LORD feel about having made man on the earth?

cards.text: The LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart. Friend, I'm setting my spatula down for this one, because then the LORD speaks.

cards.question: The LORD is grieved that He made man. What does the LORD say He will do?

answers.text: Blot out man from the earth

cards.question: The LORD says He will blot out man from the face of the earth. True or false: His words are only about man and leave out the animals and birds.

cards.text: Every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air. And then one little word turns the whole page: however.

cards.question: The LORD is grieved over man and says He will blot him out. Then comes the word however. True or false: Noah finds favor in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Keep that name close, friend. The oven timer on this story hasn't even dinged yet.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice cards (3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 14) against 2 fill in the blank (6, 11) and 2 true or false (15, 17).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke "this photo album just got a WHOLE lot more interesting" comes right after the sons of God and the daughters of men having children together. Coming at that moment, it reads as innuendo.

rule.text: No cursing, crude humor, innuendo, or social or political commentary.

findings.problem: "I'm holding my breath like the junk drawer just slid open" depends on knowing that the drawer's residents held their breath whenever it opened. That detail is in Papa Dorin's backstory, not in this lesson. A baker who doesn't know it would say "huh?"

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Card 13 retells that the LORD "was grieved in His heart." Card 12 just asked and answered that, so this part of the card is a recap.
Card 16 opens by restating "Every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air." Card 15 just answered that. The line is also a fragment with no context.

Card 18 holds only the line saying the story isn't over and tells no part of the passage. Every story card must tell part of the passage and move it forward. But 6:8, the last verse, was already answered on card 17, so retelling it here would be a recap.
findings.question: When the last verse of a passage is covered by a choice card, what should the final story card carrying the 'story isn't over' line contain? Can it be only that line, or should the walkthrough be arranged so the last verse is told on that story card instead of asked?
